   rounds, the analyzer must compare every panel that SHOULD have changed,
   not just the first. The plan's §5 Risk row 3 already names this; keep the
   plan's wording ("compare to the corresponding field in the NEW round's
   result JSON" — not "compare the whole points blob").

2. **[Statistics Claude] `points` sidecar truncation cap.** `paper_plots.py`
   caps embedded rows at `_MAX_SIDECAR_ROWS` (writes `truncated`/`total_points`).
   The cross-check therefore samples a truncated view — catches wholesale
   wrong-source-JSON staleness (#667 class), but would not catch staleness
   confined to a truncated-away point. Worth a half-sentence noting truncated
   sidecars compare only the embedded subset.
